entries.notes: l.258 against EGF.IsUniversalFamilyEps. The TeX quantifies over probability distributions mu, nu << lambda with bounded density and every eps > 0, and asks for a flow in the family from F_init = nu to F_term = mu with delta F_init(S) + delta F_term(S) < eps. The Lean quantifies over IsProbabilityMeasure mu, nu, mu, nu << lam, and an essential bound on rnDeriv for each (exists C, ae rnDeriv <= C). It quantifies over every eps : R>=0-inf with 0 < eps, which is equivalent to real eps > 0. It asks for some F in the family with initialError F.policy F.outflow nu mu univ + terminalError F.policy F.outflow nu mu univ < eps. So initial = nu and terminal = mu, in the same order. The two definitions agree clause for clause. The disclosed clause 'where delta F_init, delta F_term are the initial and terminal errors defined in Section ref{sec:theory1}' is correct. sec:theory1 is subsection 3.2 'Quantitative Sampling Theorem' (main.aux: newlabel{sec:theory1}{{3.2}...}), and its Definition 3.7 (l.327) defines delta F_init := (F_init + F_in - F_term - F_out)^- and delta F_term := (...)^+. Those are EGF.initialError and EGF.terminalError: initialError_eq_negPart and terminalError_eq_posPart are the Jordan parts. The clause is a notation pointer, not a hypothesis. It is needed because Definition 3.2 now uses the errors four pages before they are defined. The pair is still written '(f_out*, pi*)', as in v1. That presupposes an outflow with a density, as everywhere in the paper; the flow the Lean builds is (pi, f+ lambda) (isUniversalFamilyEps_of_policy). Refutation EGF.exact_universality_fails: the Coin family on Bool is a family of EGFs (moves id and not, topologically ergodic). It contains the summably mixing resampling kernel, and its outflows are dense in the non-negative cone. It is IsUniversalFamilyEps and not IsUniversalFamily. Under the corrected definition it is universal (Coin.isUniversalFamilyEps_family), so it no longer contradicts Theorem 3.4. C-18's second site, l.809 (v1 l.774) 'The following theorem implies Theorem ref{theo:universality}', was left unchanged, rightly. With the epsilon definition the conclusion of Theorem B.1 is the predicate of Definition 3.2, which OQ-50's own text says makes l.774 hold. What remains is routine or belongs to another entry. Bounded densities are in L^2 on a finite lambda. From one universal policy to the family is EGF.isUniversalFamilyEps_of_policy: the defect is 2-Lipschitz in the outflow in total variation, and IsDenseNonnegConeL2.isL1DenseBoundedNonneg gives L^2 => L^1. v2 does not write this step, as v1 did not. B.1's 'ergodic on (S, lambda)' follows from Theorem 3.4's summable mixing in the invariant-set sense (EGF.isKernelErgodic_of_isSummablyL2Mixing), but not in Walters' sense (lambda pi = lambda). That gap is C-22, now superseded by C-29 and C-39, which restate both theorems under one hypothesis. l.809 is therefore true as worded under the corrected definition, and no edit is owed here.

l.258 'for any two probability distributions mu, nu << lambda with bounded density' is the IsProbabilityMeasure mu, IsProbabilityMeasure nu binders of EGF.IsUniversalFamilyEps and EGF.IsUniversalFamily. The applied text is C-19's corrected text verbatim. The edit shares one sentence with C-18 and carries its own marker, l.260 '% EGF-C19'. Refutation EGF.not_isUniversalFamilyUnnormalized uses nu = lambda and mu = 2 lambda on a finite lambda != 0. No pair of probability measures has that form, so the new definition excludes the instance. hypotheses_ok is false only on the register's side. C-19's kind is missing-hypothesis, and the edit adds exactly the restriction 'mu, nu are probability measures' to the definiens. Yet `added_hypotheses` is []. Either list it, or record that it is the reading of 'distributions' ruled by OQ-49 (DEC-141). See findings.

l.287 against EGF.universality: [IsFiniteMeasure lam], any set F of generative flows, pi with IsSummablyL2Mixing pi lam, D with every f in D giving (pi, ofReal(f) lam) in F (hD), and IsDenseNonnegConeL2 lam D, conclude IsUniversalFamilyEps lam F. Hypothesis by hypothesis: lambda finite is the standing assumption of l.161. 'A parameterized family of EGF' is narrower than any set of flows, so the Lean is weaker there. 'Contains some summably L^2-mixing pi*' is hmix, with membership given by hD on the non-empty D (density puts 0 in its closure). 'The set of f_out* such that (pi*, f_out*) is in the family' is D: take D to be that set. Its elements are non-negative, so ofReal f = f. 'Dense in the non-negative cone of L^2(S, lambda)' is IsDenseNonnegConeL2: every g in L^2 with g >= 0 is an L^2-limit of a.e.-strongly measurable elements of D. An a.e.-non-negative class has an everywhere non-negative representative, so the two agree. Pi Markov comes from membership. The conclusion is 'universal' in the epsilon sense of l.258, which is IsUniversalFamilyEps. Lean >= paper, and the conclusions are equal. Refutations: EGF.not_dense_L2_of_nonneg makes the printed hypothesis unsatisfiable for non-negative outflows on lambda != 0, while the cone hypothesis is satisfiable (Coin.isDenseNonnegConeL2_D, fixedPolicyFamily), so the theorem is no longer vacuous. EGF.Coin.allOutflows_reading_fails: in familyAll the only outflow paired with the mixing pol is lambda, density 1, which is not dense in the cone. The new hypothesis therefore excludes the instance. hypotheses_ok is false on the register's side. The pairing 'such that (pi*, f_out*) is in the family' is an added hypothesis against the 'all outflows' reading, which the entry refutes (its refutation lists Coin.allOutflows_reading_fails). Yet C-20's `added_hypotheses` is [] and its finding does not mention the pairing. The finding is also stale: 'Theorem 3.4 itself is not yet derived from Theorem B.1 in Lean', while EGF.universality is C-20's anchor. See findings.

l.276. 'phi pi^n := d((phi lambda) pi^n)/d lambda' is EGF.transfer: the rnDeriv against lam of pushIter pi n (lam.withDensity ofReal(phi)) minus that of the negative part. Under the definition's own hypothesis (lambda-hat pi = lambda-hat, lambda-hat ~ lambda), (phi+- lambda) pi^n << lambda-hat pi^n = lambda-hat << lambda. The signed measure (phi lambda) pi^n is finite because phi is in L^2 of a finite lambda, hence in L^1. So the TeX Radon-Nikodym derivative exists and equals the Lean difference of rnDerivs (the Lean takes the absolutely continuous part unconditionally, so it is more general). 'H = {phi in L^2(lambda) : ||phi||_{L^2(lambda)} = 1 and int_S phi d lambda = 0}' is EGF.unitMeanZero: MemLp phi 2 lam, eLpNorm phi 2 lam = 1, and int phi dlam = 0. 'gamma_n = sup_H int (phi pi^n)^2 d lambda-hat', unchanged, is EGF.mixingCoeff pi lam lamHat n (in [0, inf]). 'Summable' is EGF.IsSummablyL2Mixing: exists lamHat, lamHat.bind pi = lamHat, lamHat << lam, lam << lamHat, and tsum gamma_n != inf. lambda-hat is any measure, not assumed finite, as printed. The applied text is C-25's corrected text and is DEC-145's ruling of OQ-47 word for word. No hypothesis is added. There is no refutation (kind gap). The one-step operator of the remark at l.283, phi |-> d((phi lambda) pi)/d lambda, is now the n = 1 case of the definition, and the Cesaro sentence at l.281 reads with it. Both are consistent.

findings.what: A use of the changed notion is left inconsistent. The Expressivity paragraph (v1 l.238, unchanged) says 'Ergodicity guarantees that the parameterized family of EGFs is able to be flow-matching for any non-zero F_init << lambda and F_term << lambda'. That is v1's exact, unnormalized universality, the two readings C-18 and C-19 have just removed from Definition 3.2. After the batch, v2 says one thing at l.258/l.287 (errors < eps, probability distributions with bounded density) and another at l.245 (exact flow matching, any non-zero masses). l.245 is also false in v2's own terms. Flow matching forces F_init(S) = F_term(S) (Theorem 2.1, l.185; EGF.not_isUniversalFamilyUnnormalized). And EGF.exact_universality_fails exhibits a family of EGFs with topologically ergodic moves, a summably mixing policy and dense outflows in which no flow is flow-matching from nu_irr to lambda, both probability measures with bounded density. The corrector was right not to edit l.245: no entry of this batch prints v1 l.238. C-29 (T-egf-correct-ergodicity) lists v1 l.238 and says it 'is right in its epsilon form', but its `corrected` text gives no l.238 sentence. As registered, nothing will ever fix it. The fix belongs to this batch's content (C-18 exact -> epsilon, C-19 non-zero -> probability), not to C-29's (which concerns 'Ergodicity guarantees', mixing against ergodicity).

findings.what: Real, but not this batch's. v1 l.664 (unchanged) reads 'from the proof of the universality Theorem ref{theo:universality}, we observe that f_out* can be obtained as a fixed point of a flow operator dependent on pi*, F_init, and F_term'. Theorem 3.4 has no proof in v1 or v2; the proof meant is that of Theorem B.1 (l.813-839), where f_out* = d(nu_infty^eta)^+/d lambda is built from the fixed point nu_infty of H. The dispatch's 'v2 l.688' is l.692 in the current working copy. This batch makes it no worse: it changes neither Theorem 3.4's status (still no proof) nor B.1's proof. C-39 (T-egf-correct-ergodicity) will, though. Once B.1's proof is the Cesaro-weighted Neumann series, no fixed point of H appears in it. Only C-21's remark (lambda invariant) keeps a convergent series sum_t (F_init - F_term) pi^t, which is a fixed point of H. The next sentence, 'This operator is a contraction for the affine toroidal family', is not formalized. H is affine with linear part nu |-> nu pi*, which is a strict contraction on mean-zero L^2(lambda) only under C-30's two-sided criterion, and on tori that rests on the cited Bekka-Guivarc'h result plus C-28 (a).

answers.disclosed_clause: Correct and harmless. ref{sec:theory1} is Section 3.2. Its Definition 3.7 (l.327) defines delta F_init and delta F_term as the negative and positive parts of F_init + F_in - F_term - F_out, which are EGF.initialError and EGF.terminalError. The clause adds no hypothesis. It should be recorded in C-18's `corrected` (finding 4).
answers.l809: True as worded under the corrected Definition 3.2: Theorem B.1's conclusion is now Definition 3.2's predicate. The step from one policy to the family is unwritten but routine (EGF.isUniversalFamilyEps_of_policy). The only residual gap is B.1's 'ergodic on (S, lambda)' read in Walters' sense. That is C-22, superseded by C-29 and C-39 in T-egf-correct-ergodicity. In the invariant-set sense, summable mixing implies it (EGF.isKernelErgodic_of_isSummablyL2Mixing). No edit is owed in this batch.
